solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Spooner's cast figure in ambitious programme

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the opening sounds of neighbouring words, so the phrase must be said with its starts exchanged

blocks.note: a cast figure is a plaster man, a statue made of plaster; swap the opening PL and M sounds

explanation.surface: A sculptor's ambitious scheme seems to involve a cast figure.
explanation.definitionFit: A master plan is an overall, far-reaching scheme, which is what an ambitious programme amounts to.

clue.text: Spot check on vehicle emissions, but not journeys

indicators.note: 'but not' tells us to take one word away from another, keeping only what is left over

blocks.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles
taken as written
missions are journeys undertaken for a purpose

explanation.surface: An inspection of exhaust fumes from a car, rather than of the trips it makes.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'check on vehicle emissions' as one phrase, but 'emissions' minus 'missions' leaves only E, added after the MOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A mote is a tiny particle or speck, the same as a spot of dust.

clue.text: Home county finally obliterated by Deep South state? That's bizarre

indicators.note: the word's final letter is wiped out, so it loses its last letter

blocks.note: Surrey is one of the Home Counties, the counties surrounding London
AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama, a Deep South state

explanation.surface: An English county wiped out by an American state would indeed be a strange event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' simply places Alabama's abbreviation beside the shortened county.
explanation.definitionFit: Surreal describes something dreamlike and weird, a close synonym of bizarre.

clue.text: Testatrix left account out of legacy, bungling way-out provision?

indicators.note: 'out of' means these letters are removed from the following word, leaving the rest
bungling handles things clumsily, so the letters end up jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the standard abbreviation for left
AC is the common abbreviation for account
taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman making her will mishandles a bequest by cutting out a bank account.
explanation.walkthrough: L and AC are taken from LEGACY, leaving EGY; those letters join TESTATRIX for the jumble. 'way-out' plays on a way out as an escape.
explanation.definitionFit: An exit strategy is a planned means of withdrawing from a situation, literally provision for a way out.

clue.text: Such as Lincoln — shot, surprised by actor

indicators.note: to be surprised by someone is to be caught by them, so one word is held inside the other

blocks.note: a player is an actor
a shot is a go, an attempt

explanation.surface: Abraham Lincoln was shot by an actor, John Wilkes Booth, and it surprised him.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln was assassinated while watching a play at Ford's Theatre, so the surface's grim history doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln was at the theatre when he was killed, making him an example of a theatregoer.

clue.text: Detective's coming up after scouring bottom of river for wader

indicators.note: scouring away the bottom of a down word removes its last letter
in a down clue, coming up means reading from bottom to top, backwards

blocks.note: the Avon is a common crossword river
TEC is short for detective; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A detective arrives after searching a riverbed for a wading bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the detective's letters behind the shortened river.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocet is a long-legged wading bird with an upturned bill.

clue.text: Services, as suppressed by church? On the contrary

indicators.note: being suppressed by something means being held down within it; 'On the contrary' swaps which word holds which

blocks.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Church services being suppressed, perhaps by a government hostile to religion.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, the church would be doing the suppressing; 'On the contrary' flips the roles, so the little word holds the church.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch, so aces are services.

clue.text: Instrument King John regularly oiled stops

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
to stop a gap is to plug it, so these letters fill the middle of another pair

blocks.note: CR is Carolus Rex, King Charles
john is slang for a toilet, as is lav
the second and fourth letters

explanation.surface: King John's instrument is kept well oiled so it plays smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'John' hides the American slang word for a toilet. King as Carolus Rex is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A clavier is a keyboard instrument such as a harpsichord or clavichord.

clue.text: Principal case of riverway observed on another planet?

indicators.note: a case is the outer covering, so only the outermost letters are kept

blocks.note: the principal performer is the star
the first and last letters
eyed means looked at, observed

explanation.surface: The main feature of a waterway seen on some other world, like canals on Mars.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'on another planet' is a figurative idiom for being unrealistic, with a nod to stars in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on another planet means being out of touch with reality, much as starry-eyed means naively idealistic.

clue.text: I end call to expose final story's contents

indicators.note: to expose something is to strip off its covering, so the outer letters go
contents are what lies inside, so only the inner letters are kept

blocks.note: to call something is to term it
the inner letters
the inner letters

explanation.surface: Someone ending a phone call in order to reveal what happens in the last instalment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I end' is what the answer might say of itself: something that terminates things.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminator is one that brings things to a close, so it could describe itself by saying it ends.

clue.text: Beast from the East driving out essentially benign priest

indicators.note: starting at the east, the right-hand side, means reading the word leftwards, backwards
the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letters are kept
driving letters out removes them from the word

blocks.note: a beast is an animal
the central two letters, its essence

explanation.surface: A dangerous creature from Asia sees off a kind-hearted holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' picks the middle of 'benign'. 'Beast from the East' was also the press name for a 2018 cold snap in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a Buddhist monk or spiritual teacher in Tibet, a kind of priest.

clue.text: Top agent in a very awkward position for surveillance

indicators.note: something awkward is ungainly and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
V is the abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: A senior spy is caught in an embarrassing predicament while watching someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A vantage point is a spot giving a commanding view, ideal for keeping watch.

clue.text: Aid to scrutinising Le Pen's spending record

indicators.note: spending something uses it up, so it is no longer there

blocks.note: taken as written
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Something to help examine the French politician's record on public spending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spending record' looks like a budget history; it is an instruction to remove a kind of record. Le Pen is a French far-right political family.
explanation.definitionFit: A lens magnifies things, helping one examine them closely.

clue.text: Old soldier re-reading novel

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters take a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A retired army man going through a favourite book again.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenadiers were soldiers originally trained to throw grenades, now a historic regiment name.

clue.text: Pipe organ parts learnt by heart

indicators.note: this verb means splits open, so one word is divided to take in the other

blocks.note: a reed is a pipe, as in an organ's reed pipe
an organ of the body may be called a member

explanation.surface: Sections of a church pipe organ that a player has memorised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' reads as a noun about organ components but is a verb: the pipe word splits to hold the organ word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something learnt by heart has been committed to memory, so it is remembered.

clue.text: Expanded terminal to accommodate fifty barges internally

indicators.note: internally points to the inside of a word, keeping its middle letters
accommodating something means giving it room inside

blocks.note: a terminal point is an end
L is fifty in Roman numerals
the inner letters

explanation.surface: A dock terminal was enlarged to take fifty barges inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlarged means made bigger, which is exactly what expanded means.

clue.text: Harvest at first failing to circulate. What could one do?

indicators.note: with the first letter failing, the word loses its opening letter
circulating means going round, so letters move from one end round to the other

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: If the harvest fails and food cannot be distributed, what hope is there?
explanation.walkthrough: The final question doubles as the definition: with no harvest, one could starve. The last two letters of the shortened word come round to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: When crops fail, going without food until death is what one might do, so the question is answered by the verb.

clue.text: Madder relative of gangland murderer presents paranoia in successive quarters

indicators.note: each of the four eight-letter words gives up one quarter, moving on a quarter each time

blocks.note: the first quarter of the word
the second quarter of the word
the third quarter of the word
the fourth quarter of the word

explanation.surface: A crazier relative of a gang killer displays paranoia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madder' reads as crazier, but it is a plant family. Each word is eight letters, so a quarter is two letters, first from the first word, second from the second, and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: The gardenia belongs to the madder family of plants, Rubiaceae, so it is a botanical relative of madder.

clue.text: List ingredients of proper ratatouille

indicators.note: ingredients are what something is made from, so the answer lies within the following words

blocks.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: A recipe listing what goes into a genuine ratatouille.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are a list of corrections to errors in a printed book.

clue.text: Extraordinary causes célèbres barring useless wanton woman

indicators.note: barring means excluding, so those letters are taken out
extraordinary means out of the usual order, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring accents
taken as written

explanation.surface: Remarkable scandals that exclude a worthless, promiscuous woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of USELESS are struck from the long phrase, leaving seven to rearrange. Rebecca de Winter in Daphne du Maurier's novel was secretly unfaithful.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of du Maurier's Rebecca was revealed as a faithless, promiscuous wife, a wanton woman.

clue.text: Poles existing chiefly on abundant generosity

indicators.note: chiefly points to the head of the word, its first letter

blocks.note: abundant means large in amount
two poles, both taken as S for South
the first letter

explanation.surface: Polish people living mainly on someone's lavish charity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' in a across clue places the earlier words after LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Largesse is generous giving of money or gifts, so it is a synonym of generosity.

clue.text: Elements of hell I've seen around Port of Spain

indicators.note: elements are component parts, so the answer is made of a run of the following letters
turning around means facing the other way, so the run is read backwards

blocks.note: found across the words

explanation.surface: Someone describing the hellish sights they have witnessed near a Spanish port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port of Spain' sounds like Trinidad's capital, but it simply means a port in Spain; Seville is an inland river port on the Guadalquivir.
explanation.definitionFit: Seville in Andalusia is a historic river port, so it is a port of Spain.

clue.text: American fellow in swimming race shows bottle

indicators.note: swimming letters move about freely, so they are rearranged
in places these letters inside the other word

blocks.note: rearranged letters of the word
A is a standard abbreviation for American
F is a standard abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: An American man in a swimming race displays his water bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass bottle or flask for serving wine or water at table.

clue.text: One making sound post-natal assessment?

blocks.note: surface reading: a doctor or midwife giving a healthy verdict on a newborn
setter's reading: something making musical sound, and the post-natal assessment is a judgment on size, small but substantial

explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' reads as healthy and 'post-natal' points to newborns; really this is a musical instrument whose name sounds like a verdict on a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small grand piano, an instrument that makes musical sound and whose name pairs an infant with an impressive rating.

clue.text: Prepare way to follow priest

blocks.note: P is an abbreviation for priest
Ave is short for avenue, a way

explanation.surface: Getting the path ready for a priest's procession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow priest' puts the way after the priest; 'pave the way' also echoes the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To pave is to lay a surface ready for use, so it means to prepare, especially in paving the way.

clue.text: Worry about being captured by us

indicators.note: something captured is held inside its captor

blocks.note: 'us' is the newspaper itself, the Financial Times
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A captive's anxiety about being held by the speakers.
explanation.walkthrough: Since the puzzle appears in the Financial Times, 'us' is that paper's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To fret is to be anxious and agitated, a synonym of worry.

clue.text: Productive sources of revenue in Capitol Hill

indicators.note: a source is where something begins, so each word gives its opening letter

blocks.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: Lucrative ways that Washington raises money.
explanation.definitionFit: Rich soil or rich seams yield plenty, so rich can mean fertile or productive.

clue.text: Old man feeling worse about decline denied special medication

indicators.note: denied means refused it, so that letter is withheld
about means surrounding, so the outer words go round

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
to sink is to decline
S is an abbreviation for special
more ill

explanation.surface: An elderly man growing sicker and declining is denied his special drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man feeling worse' reads as one phrase, and the father and the comparative wrap around the shortened decline.
explanation.definitionFit: A painkiller is a drug that relieves pain, a type of medication.

clue.text: Implicitly relaxed face

indicators.note: the word 'back' is implied rather than stated: relaxed means laid-back, so read the word back

blocks.note: relaxed is laid-back, and the first part of that phrase is used

explanation.surface: A calm expression that only hints at a person's ease.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversal signal is hidden inside the synonym: laid-back, so the first word is taken backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A dial is the face of a clock or watch, and also slang for a person's face.

clue.text: Nothing in carriage needs changing for active service unit

indicators.note: changing one thing for another swaps it out, so one letter is replaced

blocks.note: carriage is bearing or deportment
O looks like zero, nothing
A is an abbreviation for active

explanation.surface: An empty railway carriage needs swapping for a military unit on active service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carriage' suggests a railway coach but means posture.
explanation.definitionFit: A department is a division or unit of an organisation providing a particular service.
